oneLiner: The largest independent GPU cloud, renting NVIDIA capacity under multi-year take-or-pay contracts and funding the build almost entirely with debt. The market is betting on whether contract-backed loans and customer prepayments can carry the build while the unsecured bond market stays shut - the equity is a thin slice on top of the lenders.

verdict.stance: Neutral - still a call on credit, odds improved
verdict.summary: Q3 answered the operating questions and left the credit one open. Margin turned a quarter ahead of plan, customer concentration fell and management laid out a 2027 funding plan that avoids the unsecured market, yet unsecured bonds still yield about 15% and interest stays above adjusted operating income through at least Q4. Net debt already exceeds the equity value and rises through 2027, so the equity swings several-fold on the EV/Sales the market pays: the bear case leaves it in the low teens, the bull case is more than ten times that. We moved up one notch from Cautious because two of three signposts were met and less of the funding now depends on reopening bond markets. We would turn Positive if the next secured loan prices at or below 7.5%, the $9B of prepayments arrives and unsecured yields fall below ~12%; we would go back to Cautious on a contract breach, a cash-trap trigger, or a parent-level raise above the $5B management capped through 2027.
wtb: Q4 2026 revenue lands at $4.7-5.0B and adjusted operating income at $750-850M (~16-17% margin), as the raised FY2026 guide implies.
FY2027 revenue reaches ~$25B (+~90%) from a $20-21B exit run-rate with capex held near the 2026 level of $37-39B.
About $9B of customer prepayments and deposits is collected by the Q4 report and parent-level capital raised through 2027 stays below $5B, with no unsecured issuance.
No customer among the top two (54% of Q3 revenue) breaches or renegotiates a contract that backs project debt through 2027.

bear.why: Prepayments fall short and secured lenders tighten, so CoreWeave slows the 2027 build to protect liquidity; revenue only holds the top of the exit-2026 run-rate (~$21B, +~60%) and a customer renegotiation or power delay hits backlog conversion. Interest stays above operating income (analysts already see ~$5.3B of 2027 interest vs ~$4.1B EBIT, per TIKR). The market values the business at ~3.5x sales on end-2027 net debt, which leaves the equity in the low teens per share.

base.why: Backlog converts on schedule: FY2027 revenue ~$25B (+~90%) from contracted deliveries plus renewals at higher prices, adjusted operating margin in the high teens and adjusted EBITDA margin above 60%. The build is funded by prepayments and secured loans at 7-7.5%, with under $5B of parent-level capital. The market pays ~4.7x FY2027 sales on end-2027 net debt - no re-rating, because growth halves and leverage is higher.

bull.why: Pricing keeps rising (+~25% in July, +~10% more late in Q3), 2027 renewals add close to $4B of annualized revenue with no capex and new short-term deals fill every megawatt, pushing FY2027 revenue to ~$29B. Margins pass 20%, unsecured bonds rally back toward their ~9.6% coupons and the market pays ~6x sales as visibility to 2028 consensus (~$44B) firms up.

scenarioModel.note: Value per share = (FY2027 revenue x EV/Sales - net debt) / shares. The page nets its data-feed net debt of ~$45B and ~551M shares; reported figures at Sep 30, 2026 were $47.5B of debt and finance leases less $4.1B of cash (~$43B net; $2.3B of restricted cash not netted). We expect more net debt by end-2027 (Siberforge estimate, unverified: ~+$20B bear, ~+$29B base, ~+$34B bull vs the page figure, from ~$9-10B of Q4 2026 capex and a 2027 build of ~$28B / ~$38B / ~$45B against ~$11B / ~$16B / ~$20B of operating cash flow including prepayments). The multiples shown are therefore the true end-2027 EV/Sales (~3.5x / ~4.7x / ~6.0x) minus that extra debt per dollar of revenue. Roughly: bear ~$14, base ~$78, bull ~$171 per share. The base estimate of extra debt is ~$5B lower than in October because management guided 2027 capex in line with 2026 on committed backlog. Dilution beyond today's count is not modelled (556M shares were outstanding at Oct 30 and the ATM allows 35M more; using ~590M would cut the base value to ~$72). Inputs are Siberforge estimates, not consensus.

debates.q: Can CoreWeave fund the 2027 build without the unsecured bond market?
debates.bull: Management says it can: about $9B of customer prepayments and deposits is expected within three months (prepayments were collected on 70% of 2026 deals), the next delayed-draw loan should price at 7-7.5% and finance more than 90% of the related capex, secured loans trade around par, and the CFO expects less than $5B of parent-level capital through 2027. Liquidity at Sep 30 was $6.5B plus nearly $5B undrawn.
debates.bear: Unsecured lenders disagree: the 9.625% 2032 notes yielded above 16% on Nov 6 and a 2030 note about 15.2% with five-year CDS near 1,135bp after the print (Reuters, via secondary coverage). Debt rose to $46.9B at Sep 30, of which $10.6B is current, Q4 interest is guided at $1.05-1.15B, and net debt is well above the equity value on the quality check.
debates.view: The plan is credible on paper because the money comes from customers and asset-level lenders who see the contracts, not from bond buyers. But it is a plan: prepayments are a forecast and the parent-level cap has not been tested. We give it better-than-even odds and want the cash to arrive before paying for more than the base case.

signpost.metric: Coupon on the next DDTL; prepayments and deposits collected; yield on unsecured 2031/2032 notes
signpost.threshold: constructive: loan at or below 7.5%, ~$9B collected, yields below ~12%; bearish: loan above ~8.5%, under $6B collected, yields above ~18% or any equity raise outside the ATM
signpost.when: Loan launch in the coming weeks; Q4 2026 report, late Feb 2027

debates.q: Does operating income outgrow the interest bill in 2027?
debates.bull: The amber margin row on the quality check is turning: adjusted operating margin doubled to 10% in Q3 from 5% in Q2 and the raised FY2026 guide implies ~16-17% in Q4. Short-term deals sell above $40M per MW a year, new 4-5 year contracts at $20-25M per MW, and management expects the adjusted net loss to narrow in 2027 and turn positive in 1H 2028.
debates.bear: Interest of $846M was still 2.2x adjusted operating income in Q3 and the Q4 guide keeps it above the implied $750-850M. The GAAP net loss widened to $709M, and analysts model 2027 interest above 2027 EBIT (TIKR). Adjusted figures exclude stock compensation that shows up as dilution.
debates.view: The margin thesis is intact and ahead of schedule; the open question moved from whether margin turns to whether it outruns debt service. We expect adjusted operating income to pass interest in 2H 2027 in the base case. A Q4 miss on the implied range would reopen the bear case.

signpost.metric: Q4 2026 adjusted operating income vs interest expense; FY2027 margin and interest guide
signpost.threshold: above $800M with interest inside $1.05-1.15B and a FY2027 guide where adjusted operating income covers interest by year-end = on track; below $700M = margin thesis slipping

debates.q: Is the backlog as good as cash?
debates.bull: Backlog rose by ~$28B in a quarter and more than half is tied to contracts with delivery starting by end-2026; the two largest customers fell to 30% and 24% of Q3 revenue (54%, from 36% and 26% in Q2) and ~90% of growth came from existing customers. NVIDIA must buy unsold capacity through Apr 2032 and management puts qualified demand through 2027 at 10x available capacity.
debates.bear: Only 36% of the $132.3B of remaining performance obligations falls due by Sep 2028; the rest runs out to 2033, long after today's GPUs are a generation or two old. Two buyers are still more than half of revenue, OpenAI's funding is not CoreWeave's to control, and a loan clause can trap cash if a customer backing a $2.6B facility breaches.
debates.view: Diversification is working but only just through our 55% threshold. The backlog is the reason the equity has value; its near-term slice (~$48B over 24 months) supports the base case, while the long tail deserves a discount. A single counterparty event remains the main path to the bear case.

signpost.metric: FY2027 revenue guide; top-two customer share; any cash-trap or contract-amendment 8-K
signpost.threshold: FY2027 guide at or above ~$24B and top-two share below 50% = base case or better; guide below ~$22B or any cash-trap event = bear case

thesis: Demand is contracted, not hoped for. Backlog is up 138% YoY, capacity is largely sold out through 2027 and NVIDIA's purchase obligation on unsold capacity through Apr 2032 puts a floor under utilisation (debate 3).

Pricing is rising, not falling. Two list-price increases in Q3 and short-term deals above $40M per MW are what turned the margin curve a quarter early; ~130,000 GPUs come off contract in 2027 and could reprice into close to $4B of annualized revenue with no new capex (debate 2).

Scale compounds. Q3 growth accelerated to +168% after four quarters near +110%, the exit-2026 run-rate guide rose to $20-21B and contracted power reached 4.6GW - first allocation of each NVIDIA generation is the moat.

Funding is shifting to customers and secured lenders. Prepayments, contract-backed delayed-draw loans at 7-7.5% and a parent-level raise capped below $5B through 2027 mean the distressed unsecured bonds are a price signal more than a funding source (debate 1).

latestProse: Q3 2026 (ended Sep 30; reported Nov 10). Revenue $3.66B, +168% YoY and +42% QoQ, above the top of guidance; adjusted EBITDA $2.26B (62% margin) and adjusted operating income $379M (10%), a double-digit margin one quarter ahead of plan, against net interest expense of $846M; GAAP operating income $207M and GAAP net loss $709M ($1.27 per share on 559M weighted shares, +12% YoY). Operating cash flow was $1.98B and cash capex $9.4B ($14.5B on management's basis, with Q4 deliveries pulled forward). Backlog reached ~$132.5B and debt $46.9B. On the call management said capacity is largely sold out through 2027, that it will not issue parent-level unsecured debt at current yields, and that committed backlog alone implies 2027 capex in line with 2026. Shares had lost about 40% in the month before the print as unsecured yields passed 16% and CDS peaked near 1,290bp (Nov 5); they rose ~24% on Nov 11. No rating-agency action was found.
guidanceProse: FY2026 raised on Nov 10: revenue $13.0-13.3B (from $12.4-13.2B), adjusted operating income $1.275-1.375B (from $960M-1.15B), capex $37-39B (low end up from $35B), exit-2026 annualized run-rate revenue $20-21B (from $18.5-19.5B), year-end active power above 1.85GW (reiterated). Q4 2026 interest expense $1.05-1.15B. Less the nine-month actuals, the guide implies Q4 revenue of ~$4.7-5.0B and adjusted operating income of ~$750-850M (Siberforge arithmetic). No FY2027 guide yet; management expects the adjusted net loss to narrow in 2027 and adjusted net income from 1H 2028.

guide.label: FY26 rev guide (raised Nov 10)
guide.sub: adj. op inc. $1.275-1.375B | capex $37-39B | exit ARR $20-21B

segments: GPU cloud (neocloud): rents NVIDIA-based AI capacity (Blackwell, Vera Rubin NVL72) under multi-year committed contracts to AI labs (OpenAI, Anthropic), hyperscalers (Microsoft, Meta) and trading firms (Jane Street, Hudson River Trading); Q3 2026 added Canva, Substack and Wayve among others.

Funding structure: mostly secured delayed-draw facilities backed by customer contracts (an $8.5B investment-grade loan in Mar 2026 carried a ~5.9% fixed tranche), plus unsecured notes (8.5-9.75% coupons), convertibles and a small non-recourse layer; ATM program for up to 35M shares.
competitive: Hyperscalers (AWS, Azure, GCP, OCI) are both customers and competitors; Microsoft and Meta keep building their own capacity alongside CoreWeave contracts.

Neoclouds: Nebius, Crusoe, Lambda, Nscale (Nvidia-backed; reported IPO plans in Aug 2026, status unverified) and Applied Digital/Iren as power-led hosts - the whole group sold off with CoreWeave in October.

On-demand prior-generation GPU pricing is fragmented, while new-generation contract pricing is rising; the spread between the two is the repricing risk - or, as in 2026, the repricing gain - at renewal.
India, Indonesia and Spain make up more than 1.3GW of contracted power (240MW India campus announced Oct 6, 2026, capacity from mid-2028), widening the footprint but adding capex before revenue.
moat: Scale, NVIDIA allocation priority and $130B+ of contracted revenue - not technology. GPUs are a commodity any rival can buy; the edge is deployment speed, access to contract-backed financing and switching friction inside multi-year commitments. The moat is only as durable as the capital markets that fund it.
risks: Credit is the binding constraint. Q3 debt proceeds were $10.3B against $2.3B of repayments and borrowing keeps rising with the 2027 build, the leverage row on the quality check is flagged, and the unsecured market is priced for distress - the funding plan works only if prepayments and secured loans arrive as described (debate 1).

Dilution is the release valve. Diluted shares rose 13.1% YoY on the quality check (stock comp, private placements of ~$3.0B in the first nine months of 2026); the ATM allows ~35M more (~6%) and the ~$4.2B of convertibles issued in Q3 add potential shares - each share owns less of a growing but leveraged business.

Interest outruns operating income. GAAP operating margin spent three quarters below zero before Q3 and debt service still exceeds adjusted operating income; a slip in the implied Q4 margin leaves no earnings cushion under the debt (debate 2).

Counterparty concentration. Two customers are more than half of revenue; OpenAI's funding capacity and a cash-trap clause on contract-backed debt link one customer's problems directly to CoreWeave's liquidity (debate 3).

Depreciation and repricing. GPUs depreciate over six years against roughly annual product cycles, capex ran at 271% of TTM revenue on the quality check, and most of the backlog falls due after Sep 2028 - renewal pricing that helps today can reverse when supply catches up.
catalysts: Nov 18, 2026 (approx.): NVIDIA Q3 FY2027 report - Vera Rubin ramp and any comment on neocloud financing (debate 1).
Nov-Dec 2026: launch and pricing of the next delayed-draw term loan, guided at 7-7.5% (debate 1).
Through Feb 2027: receipt of ~$9B of customer prepayments and deposits; unsecured bond yields and CDS as the daily read (debate 1).
Late Feb 2027: Q4 2026 report and first FY2027 guide - revenue, capex, interest and the funding plan (debates 1, 2, 3).

valPresets.note: FCF-based DCF is meaningless while TTM FCF is about -$20B. This mode grows revenue, applies a horizon FCF margin and an exit multiple, and nets off today's debt. Interim burn and future dilution are ignored -- generous to every case.
